body.html: Background
body.text: Background

items.html: Safeguarding national sovereignty, security, and development interests is a constitutional responsibility of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (HKSAR). On 30 June 2020, the Standing Committee of the National People’s Congress enacted the Law of the People’s Republic of China on Safeguarding National Security in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (hereinafter referred to as the “Hong Kong National Security Law”), which was promulgated and implemented in Hong Kong on the same day by being listed in Annex III to the Basic Law in accordance with Article 18 of the Basic Law.

Pursuant to Article 12 of the Hong Kong National Security Law, the HKSAR establishes the Committee for Safeguarding National Security (hereinafter referred to as the “CSNS”), which is responsible for affairs relating to safeguarding national security in the HKSAR, assumes the primary responsibility for safeguarding national security, and is subject to the supervision of and accountability to the Central People’s Government. The CSNS is assisted by a National Security Adviser designated by the Central People’s Government (Article 15). The Hong Kong National Security Law also provides for the establishment of a Secretariat of the CSNS (Article 13), a department for safeguarding national security within the Police Force (hereinafter referred to as the “Police National Security Department”) (Article 16), and a specialized prosecution division within the Department of Justice for national security offences (hereinafter referred to as the “National Security Prosecutions Division of the Department of Justice”) (Article 18). Articles 14, 17, and 18 of the Hong Kong National Security Law clearly set out the respective duties of the CSNS, the Police National Security Department, and the National Security Prosecutions Division of the Department of Justice.

Pursuant to Article 19 of the Hong Kong National Security Law, with the approval of the Chief Executive, the Financial Secretary shall allocate from the general revenue of the Government a dedicated fund to meet expenditure related to safeguarding national security (hereinafter referred to as the “Dedicated Fund”) and approve the establishment of posts involved, free from the restrictions of the existing laws of the HKSAR. The Financial Secretary shall submit to the Legislative Council an annual report on the control and management of the Dedicated Fund.

body.html: Control and Management of the Dedicated Fund
body.text: Control and Management of the Dedicated Fund

items.html: The funding arrangements for expenditure on safeguarding national security in the HKSAR have been made strictly in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Hong Kong National Security Law. Having regard to the approved establishment of the relevant bodies and their estimates of recurrent and non-recurrent expenditure required for the discharge of duties related to safeguarding national security, the Financial Secretary allocated HK$8 billion from the Government’s general revenue as the Dedicated Fund in December 2020 in accordance with the aforesaid provisions, and subsequently allocated a further HK$5 billion from the general revenue in March 2023 for meeting expenditure related to safeguarding national security.

Article 51 of the Hong Kong National Security Law stipulates that the funding of the Office for Safeguarding National Security of the Central People’s Government in the HKSAR (hereinafter referred to as the “Office for Safeguarding National Security”) shall be borne by the Central Government. Accordingly, the total allocation of HK$13 billion mentioned above does not involve any funding for the Office for Safeguarding National Security.

In view of the special and confidential nature of work relating to safeguarding national security, the Secretariat of the CSNS has established a dedicated accounting and finance team (hereinafter referred to as the “Finance Team”) to handle income and expenditure arrangements and financial matters relating to such work, and to report directly to the Financial Secretary. The accounting policies, financial policies, and preparation of financial statements adopted by the Finance Team are consistent with the policies and practices customarily adopted by the HKSAR Government.

This paper sets out the report on the control and management of the Dedicated Fund for the year 2024. Expenditure from the Dedicated Fund during the reporting period is classified into two main categories:

(i) Recurrent expenditure – including salaries and allowances, fees for engagement of specialized services, rent, and other operating and administrative expenses; and
(ii) Non-recurrent expenditure – including minor building works, specialized equipment, system set-up, machinery and vehicles, and other capital expenditure.

Income during the reporting period mainly comprised interest income from deposits. During the reporting period, no additional injection of funds into the Dedicated Fund was made by the HKSAR Government.

To strengthen oversight of the use and management of the Dedicated Fund, the Financial Secretary arranged for an independent financial audit of the relevant accounts to ensure that the accounts and financial statements prepared by the Finance Team are accurate and proper, and comply with reasonably applicable accounting policies and standards.

The Financial Secretary has reviewed the financial statements for the year 2024 prepared in respect of the Dedicated Fund and audited independently, and has noted that the independent auditor agreed that the financial statements were prepared, in all material respects, in accordance with the requirements of Article 19 of the Hong Kong National Security Law, adopting and consistently applying reasonable and applicable accounting policies and standards. The independent auditor conducted the audit in accordance with Hong Kong Standards on Auditing and issued an unqualified audit opinion on the financial statements.

Pursuant to Article 14 of the Hong Kong National Security Law, the work of the CSNS is not subject to interference by any institution, organization, or individual in the HKSAR, and information relating to its work shall not be disclosed. Accordingly, no further disclosure will be made regarding the detailed use of the Dedicated Fund. In fact, many jurisdictions regard expenditure and staffing establishments relating to national security as highly confidential information and do not disclose detailed information on such expenditure.

body.html: One day after Legislative Council members criticised the requirement that professional qualifications and Hong Kong SAR passports of fugitives could only be revoked six months after a court warrant is issued as being overly “compassionate,” the Secretary for Security stated that the government would “actively consider” removing the six-month condition. At the end of last year, police also issued a wanted notice for Agnes Chow, dubbed the “Hong Kong democracy goddess,” for absconding while on bail. To date, none have been apprehended. body.text: [Ming Pao Exclusive] On the third day after legislation under Article 23 of the Basic Law came into effect, its first enforcement case emerged. The new Article 23 regime tightens the threshold for early release of prisoners convicted of national security offences, requiring proof that their release would not be detrimental to national security before any sentence reduction may be granted.

Thank you.

body.html: Chief Executive: Thank you. First, regarding the ground subsidence at the Man Kam To boundary crossing, which has caused some unevenness on the ground surface, we are very concerned about this. The Secretary for Transport and Logistics has already explained that our food supply from Mainland China will not be affected. Although northbound traffic through Man Kam To has been affected, many vehicles can pass through other crossings, including the Liantang/Heung Yuen Wai boundary crossing, to travel north. Of course, we hope to repair the Man Kam To crossing as soon as possible, as cross-boundary clearance is very important to our overall trade. We have communicated with the relevant Mainland Chinese authorities, who are actively addressing the actual situation. I hope this can be resolved as soon as possible, but according to preliminary information, it may take about a month, or longer — measured in months. We will maintain communication with them and will inform the public, particularly the trade sector, as soon as information becomes available.

body.html: Secretary for Security: Fellow Hong Kong citizens, members of the press. First, I would like to add some remarks regarding the Police's further wanting of five fugitives yesterday (December 14). First, during their time at large, these five “runaway” fugitives have continued to engage in conduct endangering national security. Such conduct includes begging foreign governments to impose “sanctions” against central and SAR officials, and even judicial officers. In addition, they have published videos suspected of inciting secession, inciting endangerment of national security, and inciting subversion of state power. They have also advocated undergoing armed training, or even organising armed forces, to resist or oppose the SAR Government, and have even promoted “Hong Kong independence.” All of this constitutes conduct in violation of the Hong Kong National Security Law and endangering national security. Our wanted-person operations are entirely based on evidence and prosecutorial policy, from which the conclusion to place them on the wanted list is derived.

body.html: These fugitives believe that by “running off” overseas they can escape legal responsibility, and one or two of the wanted persons even rely on holding foreign passports, believing there is nothing we can do about them. I want to tell everyone: the Hong Kong National Security Law has an extraterritorial effect – no matter where you violate the Hong Kong National Security Law, and no matter how long you wait, you remain a wanted person. At this moment, a foreign government may be protecting and shielding you because you are their “running dog” – but once you lose your use value, you will become a discarded pawn; you will remain a wanted person forever, unable to see the light like a rat crossing the street, and you will bring shame upon your family and leave them disgraced.

body.html: The Secretary for Security, Mr Chris Tang, held a press conference this morning (December 24) on the specification of persons wanted on suspicion of committing offences endangering national security as absconders and the related specified measures. The Deputy Commissioner of Police (National Security), Mr Kan Kai-yan, and the Chief Superintendent of the National Security Department, Mr Li Kwai-wah, also attended. body.text: The Secretary for Security, Mr Chris Tang, held a press conference this morning (December 24) on the specification of persons wanted on suspicion of committing offences endangering national security as absconders and the related specified measures. The Deputy Commissioner of Police (National Security), Mr Kan Kai-yan, and the Chief Superintendent of the National Security Department, Mr Li Kwai-wah, also attended. The following is the opening statement given at the press conference:

body.html: Secretary for Security: Fellow Hong Kong citizens, members of the press, good morning to you all. Today the SAR Government is taking further action against persons who have absconded overseas and continue to engage in conduct and activities endangering national security.
body.text: Secretary for Security: Fellow Hong Kong citizens, members of the press, good morning to you all. Today the SAR Government is taking further action against persons who have absconded overseas and continue to engage in conduct and activities endangering national security.

body.html: First, I announce that I have exercised the powers conferred on me under the Safeguarding National Security Ordinance, and have today published a notice in the Gazette specifying seven persons – previously wanted in July and December 2023, who have absconded overseas and against whom the courts have issued arrest warrants on suspicion of committing offences endangering national security, namely Kwok Fung-yee (Anna Kwok), Yuan Gong-yi (Elmer Yuen), Wing-hang Kwok (Dennis Kwok), Chi-fung Hui (Ted Hui), Kin-fung Yam (Kevin Yam), Hui Wing-ting (Frances Hui), and Joey Siu – as absconders, and have specified the measures to be applied against these seven absconders.

body.html: These persons who endanger national security, after absconding overseas, have continued to engage in activities endangering national security, including advocating “Hong Kong independence” through social media platforms and the overthrow of the fundamental system of the People’s Republic of China established under the Constitution of the People’s Republic of China, and inciting secession; launching so-called “referendums” in an attempt to implement so-called “self-determination” and inciting subversion of state power; and publishing so-called reports and meeting with foreign politicians and government officials to request “sanctions,” blockades, and other hostile actions against China and the Hong Kong SAR, including "sanctions" against central and SAR officials and prosecutors.

body.html: Furthermore, in relation to one of the absconders specified today, Chi-fung Hui, he conspired with foreign politicians to forge documents in order to deceive the court into permitting him to leave Hong Kong, when in fact he absconded overseas. Following investigation, the Department of Justice considers that there is sufficient evidence to prove that Chi-fung Hui has committed offences endangering national security and has profited therefrom, including receiving and profiting from funds on an online platform suspected of being used to commit offences endangering national security. In this regard, the Department of Justice will, pursuant to paragraph 9 of Schedule 3 to the Implementation Rules for Article 43 of the Law of the People’s Republic of China on Safeguarding National Security in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, commence legal proceedings to confiscate his criminal proceeds. The Police have today published a notice in the newspapers addressed to Chi-fung Hui concerning the arrest warrant against him, and the Department of Justice will shortly apply to the Court of First Instance for a confiscation order to confiscate Chi-fung Hui's criminal proceeds, in order to prevent him from using such proceeds to continue engaging in conduct and activities endangering national security.

body.html: I must emphasise that endangering national security is a very serious offence, and such conduct or activities may lead to extremely serious consequences. Under Article 37 of the Hong Kong National Security Law, the Law applies to permanent residents of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, and to companies and organisations, whether incorporated or unincorporated, established in the SAR, who commit offences under the Law outside the SAR. The Hong Kong Police therefore have a duty to pursue, in accordance with the law, persons suspected of committing offences under the Hong Kong National Security Law outside Hong Kong.

body.html: The first is Ka-man (Carmen) Lau, a 29-year-old woman, suspected of committing “incitement to secession” under Article 21 and “collusion with a foreign country or with external elements to endanger national security” under Article 29 of the Hong Kong National Security Law. During the period from October 2021 to May 2024, it is alleged that, in her capacity as a key member of the Hong Kong Democracy Council, she published articles and speeches, and posted content and videos on social media, advocating the separation of the Hong Kong SAR from the People’s Republic of China. She also begged foreign officials, legislators, and politicians to impose “sanctions,” blockades, and other hostile actions against the People's Republic of China and the Hong Kong SAR, including demanding “sanctions” against SAR government officials involved in implementing the Safeguarding National Security Ordinance, and the abolition of the privileges of Hong Kong’s economic and trade offices in other jurisdictions.

body.html: UK authorities recently charged three men under national security laws, including Yuen Chung-biu (Bill Yuen), an administrative manager at the Hong Kong ETO in London. The three are accused of assisting a foreign intelligence service in gathering intelligence and conducting surveillance, targeting individuals including Nathan Law and others subject to bounty warrants issued by the Hong Kong government. They are also alleged to have been involved in foreign interference, including forcibly entering a residential property in the United Kingdom.
